methods.description: Compare eight native Atlas counties to retained 2018/2025/2026 Census county-equivalent polygons, verify identity/tier and perform equal-area IoU/area screening; invalid Census references are repaired only in-memory for overlap triage.
methods.units: IoU fraction; projected area km²; source area attributes retained as source units
methods.area_method: Shapely polygon area after pyproj EPSG:6933 transform; temporary make_valid only for invalid Census comparator inputs

methods.description: Verify 57 issue-pinned whole-file SHA-256 values and byte counts in both working tree and declared immutable base before reading geographic calculation inputs; check the complete decompressed/reserve phase against 256 MiB; refuse duplicate and incomplete source rosters before indexing.
methods.software: Python 3.12.14 standard library hashlib/json/gzip/subprocess; exact candidate reproducer SHA is checked before every run

methods.description: Run the full guarded calculation into two distinct exclusive output directories; compare every per-run file digest and verify equality.

conclusions.text: All eight issue IDs are present in their pinned Atlas containing files and retained 2018, 2025 and 2026 Census county/equivalent responses; names, state/county codes, county tier and Georgia parent agree. The full Atlas part registry scan found 49,625 unique IDs.

The previously reported coastal and three invalid-Census-reference statistical comparison values reproduced deterministically from retained input bytes. The comparison does not prove coastal completeness or legal lines.

The retained Census 2026 layer metadata is one LF longer than the existing retrieval receipt representation; removing the LF yields exactly the receipt byte count/hash while parsed JSON stays equal. This corrects the raw-byte identity statement only.

The legal treatment and completeness of offshore water, tidal water, marsh, submerged land, and every island component for the five coastal counties remain unresolved; no authoritative dispositive survey was established.
Schley, Pike, and Terrell Census comparison rings remain invalid across retained vintages; this packet does not establish an authoritative replacement geometry or justify changing Atlas geometry.
